architecture.title: Layered architecture
architecture.description: How the code is organized, the dependency rules between layers and the flows that shape the application. This is the starting point for knowing where each kind of feature belongs.

layers.title: Layer overview
layers.description: Each layer has a single, isolated responsibility. Upper layers import from lower ones, never the other way around.

dependencies.title: Dependency rules
dependencies.description: The contract that keeps the layers decoupled and predictable.

structure.title: Folder structure
structure.description: Physical layout of the source code.

init.title: Startup flow
init.description: What happens from bootstrap until the application is mounted.

routes.title: Route composition
routes.description: Routes discovered automatically per module, with no central registry.
routes.intro: The router loads the routes.ts files from app/ and modules/ through import.meta.glob. Just create a routes.ts in the module — no central file needs to be edited.
routes.showcaseDescription: Each module exports its routes with lazy loading and meta fields.

http.title: HTTP layer
http.intro: All communication goes through a factory built on ofetch. Services live in the module that uses them (in shared/api/services only when shared), and views consume them through TanStack Query queries — they never call endpoints directly.

state.title: Global state
state.description: Pinia stores with a single responsibility.

layers.app: Startup, providers, base routes and global screens.
layers.modules: Features by domain, independent from each other.
layers.shared: Reusable cross-cutting infrastructure (api, stores, ui, utils).
layers.core: Foundation with no UI dependencies: configuration/env and constants.
layers.test: Automated validation — unit and integration tests (Vitest).
layers.e2e: End-to-end tests (Playwright) against the running application.

step1.title: main.ts creates the Vue instance
step1.description: The application is created with App.vue as its root.

step2.title: registerPlugins
step2.description: Registers Pinia → i18n → Router → Vuetify, in that order.

step3.title: Route auto-discovery
step3.description: The Router loads every routes.ts through import.meta.glob('{'@'}/{'{'}app,modules{'}'}/**/routes.ts').

step4.title: mount #app
step4.description: The application is mounted on the root element.

stores.notification: Notification queue for the global snackbar (useNotify).

onboarding.title: Getting started and building a feature
onboarding.description: Start by setting up your local environment, then follow the step-by-step guide to build a complete feature — from the module to the tests, following the template's patterns.

setup.title: Initial setup
setup.description: Clone the repository, install the dependencies and make sure the environment works.

canonical.title: Canonical example
canonical.description: The customers module implements a full CRUD across the template layers: a paginated list with search in the URL, detail, create, edit and delete. In pnpm dev, the API comes from an in-memory simulation (ADR-0039).

module.title: Create the module
module.description: Create the module folder at src/modules/{'<'}name{'>'}/ with routes.ts, views/ and components/. The route is registered automatically by the router (auto-discovery through a glob).

types.title: Create the types
types.description: Create the domain contracts in src/modules/{'<'}name{'>'}/types.ts. Only move them to src/types/ when a second module needs them (ADR-0025).

service.title: Create the service
service.description: Create the functions that talk to the backend in src/modules/{'<'}name{'>'}/api/, accepting an optional signal to cancel the request. Views never call endpoints directly.

query.title: Create the query
query.description: Server data is read with TanStack Query (ADR-0027). Wrap the query in a module composable; it handles caching, loading, errors and cancellation.

view.title: Create the container view
view.description: The view consumes the query and passes the data, the loading state and the error to presentational components.

components.title: Create presentational components
components.description: Pure components: they receive props and emit events, with no fetching and no store.

tests.title: Write tests
tests.description: Cover the service with a unit test (Vitest) and the main flow with an E2E test (Playwright).

validate.title: Validate
validate.description: Before committing, make sure lint, build and tests pass with no errors.

checklistSection.title: Completion checklist
checklistSection.description: Before opening the PR, confirm that every item is done.

checklist.routes: routes.ts typed as RouteRecordRaw[] with meta fields
checklist.e2eTest: E2E test covering the main flow

faqSection.title: Frequently asked questions
faqSection.description: The most common questions from people getting started.

sharedLogic.question: Where should logic shared between modules go?
sharedLogic.answer: In shared/ — pure logic goes in utils/, logic that talks to a store/service goes in helpers/, and reactive logic goes in composables/.

store.question: Do I need a store for my feature?
store.answer: Not for server data: use TanStack Query (ADR-0027). Create a store only for cross-cutting or persistent client state. Local screen state stays in a ref/reactive inside the component.

crossModule.question: Can I import from another module?
crossModule.answer: No. Modules are independent. If something needs to be shared, move it to shared/.

env.question: Where do environment variables live?
env.answer: Always in src/core/config/index.ts (alias {'@'}core/config). Never use import.meta.env directly.

components.title: Components & UI
components.description: Live showcase of the Vuetify components used in the template, with the usage code alongside. The rule is simple: always prefer a Vuetify component over raw HTML with custom CSS.

palette.title: Theme palette
palette.description: Semantic colors defined in app/providers/vuetify.ts. Use the names, never loose hex values.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.description: v-btn covers primary, secondary and icon actions. Vary them by variant and color.
buttons.showcaseDescription: The visual hierarchy comes from the variant (flat, tonal, outlined, text).

chips.title: Chips and badges
chips.description: v-chip for tags, statuses and compact metadata.
chips.showcaseDescription: They reinforce meaning using the theme colors.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: v-alert communicates feedback and states to the user.
alerts.showcaseDescription: The type sets the color and icon automatically.

apiError.title: API error (RFC 9457)
apiError.description: Standardize API error feedback from the Problem Details body (application/problem+json).
apiError.intro: APIs return errors in the application/problem+json format. The getErrorMessage helper extracts detail/title from the body and builds the message shown in the v-alert. Reference:
apiError.showcaseTitle: Alert from a Problem Details body
apiError.showcaseDescription: The message comes from the detail field of the error body, with the HTTP status appended.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: v-card structures content with an item, text and actions.

conventions.title: Conventions
conventions.description: The commit conventions and the code review checklist adopted in the project. Git hooks validate commit messages automatically — the checklist guides the review of every Pull Request.

branches.title: Branch naming
branches.description: Every branch starts from develop and follows the type/{'<'}optional-code{'>'}-slug pattern in kebab-case.
branches.createFrom: Always create the new branch from the latest
branches.updated: and open the PR (pull request) against

commitFormat.title: Commit format
commitFormat.description: Conventional Commits with the description in Portuguese, in the imperative mood, up to 72 characters and with no trailing period.

commitTypes.title: Commit types
commitTypes.description: They define the nature of the change. Written in English (a technical convention).
commitTypes.refactor: Code change with no change in external behavior
commitTypes.build: Build system and dependencies (Vite, scripts, tsconfig)
commitTypes.wip: Partial progress on a work branch; rewrite before the PR

scopes.title: Common scopes
scopes.description: They identify the affected layer or module. Optional when the change is cross-cutting.

examples.title: Examples
examples.description: Good messages follow the pattern; bad ones fail the hook validation (Husky).

review.title: Code review checklist
review.description: Blocking items prevent approval; suggestions are non-blocking improvements.

items.layer: Code is in the right layer (app/modules/shared/core/types)
items.noCrossModule: A module does not import from another module
items.sharedIsolation: Shared imports from neither modules nor app
items.envConfig: No direct access to import.meta.env outside core/config
items.containers: Views orchestrate data, components are presentational

items.typedProps: Props and emits typed with defineProps{'<'}T{'>'}() and defineEmits{'<'}T{'>'}()
items.centralized: Types centralized in src/types/ (not repeated inline)
items.noPrefix: Interfaces in PascalCase, without an I prefix

items.unit: Every new business rule has a unit test
items.e2e: Critical flows (auth, payment) have E2E tests

items.tokens: Tokens are never exposed in logs, templates or URLs
items.sensitive: Sensitive data is not persisted without need
items.validation: Input is validated before being sent to the backend
items.sanitize: Data shown with v-html is sanitized (if used)

items.lint: Lint passes with no errors (pnpm lint)
items.build: Build passes with no errors (pnpm build)

items.singleResponsibility: The PR does not mix unrelated responsibilities

principles.title: Guiding principles
principles.description: They guide design decisions throughout the code.
principles.srp: Single Responsibility: each unit does one thing only.
principles.dry: Don't Repeat Yourself: extract duplication into shared.
principles.kiss: Keep It Simple: prefer the simplest solution that works.
principles.soc: The (container) view orchestrates the data; the presentational component only receives props and emits events, with no access to services or stores.
principles.failFast: Validate early, fail early (config, types, guards).

decisions.title: Architectural decisions
decisions.description: The project's relevant decisions are recorded as ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) in {path}. Each one preserves the context, the alternatives and the consequences — the "why" behind the choices.

madr.title: The MADR format
madr.description: Every ADR follows a lean, readable structure.

context.title: Context
context.description: The problem and the forces behind the decision.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: The choice made and its rationale.

status.title: Status lifecycle
status.description: An ADR is never deleted — to reverse it, a new one is created that supersedes the previous one.
status.proposed: Under discussion, not yet in effect.
status.deprecated: No longer applies, with no replacement.

index.title: ADR index
index.footer: Full files in {path}. New decisions follow the sequential numbering (e.g. {example}).
